findings.title: Call to undefined isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, and AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator do not define a no-argument method with that name. The only method added by this PR is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). This is a compile error, so the services module cannot build. The call should pass context.getUser() or use a correctly defined passkeys-enabled helper.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys are no longer rendered when the user is unidentified
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false when user is null (line 161), but fillContextForm() is now gated on this helper both in authenticate() at line 115 and in the error challenge override at line 137. Before this change, authenticate() filled conditional WebAuthn when context.getUser() was null and challenge(error, field) explicitly filled only when context.getUser() == null. On the first username/password page, after a username-only submission, and after a failed password while the user is still unidentified, fillContextForm() is therefore not called, so the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID, and ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attributes are absent. Discoverable passkeys will not auto-fill/one-tap and the webauth form is missing, breaking first-login passkey flows and tests that expect //form[@id='webauth'] on those pages. The fill condition must remain true for passkeys-enabled realms even when no user is identified, while also running for known re-authenticating users.
